architecture_problem: WP206 deliberately uses a restart-stable path/device/inode authority receipt. That avoids false restart failure caused by mutable whole-file fingerprints, but same-inode writes do not alter this stable authority identity. A live mutation sensor must therefore remain separate from authority identity and must not turn unrelated canonical writes into false checkpoint corruption.

mapped_boundaries.reason: This answers which durable file is authoritative, not whether its data changed. Folding data_version/schema_version into this receipt would conflate identity with mutable state and break restart comparability.

mapped_boundaries.current: No explicit same-connection PRAGMA data_version sampling surface exists.
mapped_boundaries.candidate: Sample PRAGMA data_version on the same long-lived store connection at bounded authority-sensitive boundaries. A change means another connection committed since the prior sample. It is an invalidation hint only.

mapped_boundaries.current: UnifiedDBFingerprint records schema_version/schema digest only during separate main-file identity fingerprinting; immutable=1 intentionally excludes uncheckpointed WAL state.
mapped_boundaries.candidate: Read PRAGMA schema_version on the live connection when a data_version change or schema-sensitive operation requires revalidation. Do not persist it as durable authority.

mapped_boundaries.current: load_checkpoint checks file identity, stored authority receipt and checkpoint digest/typed replay.
mapped_boundaries.candidate: If foreign-writer drift is observed, execute the existing row digest + typed replay checks from a fresh SQLite transaction/snapshot. Abort only on a concrete checkpoint/schema/provenance mismatch, not merely because unrelated data changed.

mapped_boundaries.current: Recovery uses BEGIN IMMEDIATE, exact checkpoint digest, path/device/inode and compare-and-swap on stored authority receipt.
mapped_boundaries.candidate: A pre-lock live drift hint may force explicit re-read after BEGIN IMMEDIATE, but the transaction-bound row/CAS checks remain authoritative. data_version itself never authorizes recovery.

mapped_boundaries.current: SQLite data_version deliberately does not change for commits made by the same connection.
mapped_boundaries.candidate: Treat store connection ownership as an explicit contract or separately instrument same-connection write provenance. Do not claim data_version detects arbitrary out-of-band use of the shared Connection object.

counterhypothesis_analysis.counterhypothesis: Existing checkpoint digest plus transaction locking already makes a live-drift witness unnecessary.
counterhypothesis_analysis.reason: For recovery after BEGIN IMMEDIATE and for simple payload tamper, existing checks are strong. The unresolved value of a drift witness is narrow: detecting that a previously observed read context became stale and forcing targeted revalidation. It should not be added unless an E3/E4 discriminator demonstrates a concrete missed case or measurable diagnostic value.

build_direction.smallest_candidate_if_E3_SUPPORTS: A tiny internal LiveSQLiteDriftWitness helper with connection-local data_version baseline and optional schema_version sample, used only to request targeted revalidation. No new dependency, DB, model call, token use or effect authority.
explicitly_rejected: Persisting PRAGMA data_version as checkpoint/recovery authority
Replacing path/device/inode receipt with mutable whole-file hash
Treating schema_version as full data revision
Reading raw main-file change counter as a WAL-safe global transaction sequence
Failing every checkpoint load merely because unrelated UnifiedDB data changed

next_evidence_gate.experiment: Deterministically reproduce: (1) foreign-connection commit changes data_version while inode stays constant; (2) same-connection commit leaves data_version unchanged; (3) schema change advances schema_version; (4) unrelated foreign write can change data_version without invalidating a protected checkpoint row. Then decide whether E4 F2 ablation is worth coordination cost.

efficiency.candidate_sql_overhead: O(1) PRAGMA reads only at selected boundaries
